why: The new await on the dynamic appStore import has no try/catch, so a failed import rejects instead of returning null; ambiguous because the same unguarded await of appStore[...] also appears in getVideoAdapters, handlePayment, deletePayment and confirm, and getCalendar is the most central one.

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) now awaits getCalendar inside an unawaited async callback, so calendar/video deletions run fire-and-forget and the surrounding try/catch cannot see their rejections; the same pattern is in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125, bookings.tsx:553 and handleCancelBooking.ts:460.
The backup-code component in BackupCode.tsx is exported as a function named TwoFactor, duplicating the TwoFactor component's name.
The disable endpoint logs 'cannot proceed with backup code login', copied from the login path.
backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '')) is an exact, case-sensitive match against lowercase hex codes; the disable endpoint repeats it at disable.ts:61.
The code is checked against a decrypted in-memory copy, nulled and written back with a plain update, so two concurrent logins with the same backup code can both succeed.
URL.createObjectURL for the backup-codes download is only revoked on the next setup call; the component has no unmount cleanup that revokes backupCodesUrl.

mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from an empty/absent destinationCalendar array and is undefined (Google createEvent:100, updateEvent:198, as the comment says); there its uses are optional-chained, and the actual unguarded dereference is EventManager.create at EventManager.ts:119 (mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration).
mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration uses optional chaining inside the branch of a ternary that already checked mainHostDestinationCalendar.
In the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, it searches destinationCalendar for externalId === externalCalendarId, which can never match; deleteEvent repeats this at line 317.
The slug spread changed from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED, so with billing enabled both slug and requestedSlug are set and with billing disabled neither is.

The Calendar interface (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221, a type declaration) now declares createEvent(event, credentialId), but the Lark (line 125) and Office365 (line 72) implementations still declare createEvent(event).
When reference.credentialId is set but the credential is neither in calendarCredentials nor found in the DB, the undefined credential is still passed to updateEvent.

getAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql (NOTHING_CONDITION at worst), so authConditions is always truthy and the filter-only and NOTHING_CONDITION branches of getBaseConditions are unreachable.
Org member user IDs are only fetched when teamsFromOrg.length > 0, so an org with no child teams loses its members' personal bookings even though teamIds includes orgId.

deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach (handleCancelBooking:488, handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:489, workflows.tsx:213/377/520/575), so cancellations may not complete.
The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or calling the scheduled_sends DELETE.
WorkflowReminder.cancelled is added as Boolean? with no default (migration adds a nullable BOOLEAN), so existing rows are null instead of false; schema/migration, not a method.
The working-hours check computes end from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so slots that run past the end of working hours pass.
Two dayjs objects are compared with ===, which compares references and is always false; it should use isSame.
A missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token', which is then persisted and breaks later refreshes.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], which become literal '[object Object]'-style keys, not wildcards; module-level const (used by parseRefreshTokenResponse at line 16), not inside a listed method. (mapped to the file's <top-level> unit, which perch reads)
key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...) is the safeParse wrapper ({success, data}) and is persisted as the credential key instead of .data.
In the sync-endpoint branch refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response, while callers such as Google (res.data) and Hubspot (HubspotToken) expect the integration's token object.
On the sync path res is a fetch Response, so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token on line 95 throws.
refreshOAuthTokens is passed credentialId where it expects the userId, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong calcomUserId.

The Salesforce token refresh checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok; this is in the getClient class-property arrow function, which methods_read does not list. (mapped to the file's <top-level> unit, which perch reads)

After refreshing and saving new tokens, jsforce.Connection is still built from the stale credentialKey.access_token/instance_url (lines 105-106); this is in getClient, which methods_read does not list. (mapped to the file's <top-level> unit, which perch reads)
appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws on an invalid body, producing a 500 instead of a 400.
retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 writes a value read earlier instead of an atomic increment; the catch block repeats it at line 195.
The OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } has no method: SMS filter, so deleteMany removes email/WhatsApp reminders with retryCount > 1.
The blacklist is lowercased but guest emails are not, so blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) is bypassed by uppercase input.
isTeamAdminOrOwner requires isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner; it should be ||.
sendAddGuestsEmails decides which attendees are new with newGuests.includes(attendee.email), but the handler passes the raw input guests (addGuests.handler.ts:168), not the filtered uniqueGuests.
uniqueGuests removes existing attendees and blacklisted emails but not duplicates within the input, so createMany can insert duplicate attendees.
multiEmailValue starts as [""] (and is reset to it), so an empty string is submitted and fails email validation.
sendAddGuestsEmails sends organizer, team and attendee emails without checking the event type's disableStandardEmails metadata.
updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) passes empty data, so updatedAt is not reliably bumped and the cache status timestamp is stale.
sed -i '' is BSD/macOS syntax and fails with GNU sed on Linux; shell script, not a method.
A plain Error is thrown for a missing or unauthorized credential, which tRPC returns as a 500 instead of a TRPCError FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND.
The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of the user's locale.
